ABOUT THIS FLIGHT

Real positions.
An extraordinary perspective.

Voyager 1 and all eight planets use bundled NASA JPL Horizons position and velocity vectors, relative to the Sun in the J2000 ecliptic frame. Dates are TDB, not UTC. Playback interpolates these state vectors with cubic Hermite curves; it is an ephemeris replay, not a live telemetry feed or a new gravity solver.

NASA prediction coverage extends from September 6, 1977 through January 1, 2100. The timeline ends at the current time and keeps moving. Reaching LIVE automatically switches to 1× wall-clock playback of predicted positions, not received telemetry. Samples are five days apart, hourly near departure, and ten minutes apart around Jupiter and Saturn. Horizons describes the pre-1981 spacecraft path as an approximate patched-conic reconstruction; later states are tracking-data fits and predictions.

Onboard and spacecraft views preserve planet angular sizes and directions. Solar-system mode enlarges planets for discovery; switch to True scale to restore physical radii. Stars are illustrative. Surface maps are NASA-imagery-based composites from Solar System Scope (CC BY 4.0), not date-specific cloud maps; axial rotation is illustrative. The detailed spacecraft is a procedural reconstruction; its antenna points toward Earth, but historical roll and instrument attitude are not reconstructed. The Sun’s disk preserves its physical angular size in onboard and True scale views; the surrounding halo is exposure-adapted camera glare, not the physical solar surface. Enlarged overview mode exaggerates celestial sizes. Live UTC-to-TDB conversion uses the current 37-second leap-second offset; future leap seconds require an offset update. No sound travels through this vacuum.

Drag to turn your view. Scroll to adjust field of view or orbit distance. Space pauses playback. Select a milestone to jump to an encounter; the timeline explores the entire mission. At 1×, one real second advances one simulated second.
